summary: Customer-side library causing NVMe I/O spikes and prolonged GPU attach latency in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customer (DataWeaveAI) reports repeated throughput degradation for their dedicated pool over the last 48h. Symptoms: long GPU attach times (~8-15s, p99 ~18s), transient p99 latency spikes for short streaming requests, and slot reservation hang that resolves after NVMe IO quiets down. Impact: customer requests are seeing ~2-3x p99 latency; sustained throughput drop during midday traffic window; customer flagged as dedicated (production workloads).

Impact: Increased customer latency and missed SLOs for p99. No broad host-level OOMs or driver crashes observed. Effect is confined to the customer's reserved pool but causes cascade to fallback routing for some routes.

Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated pool: dwai-reserved-12, node type: g-p4d-24; sidecar version: 1.7.3-customer; allocator revision: 2026-03-09.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 13:05 UTC: first automated alert (p99 > 2s) observed on customer routes
- 2026-03-09 13:08 UTC: customer opened initial support chat with logs attached
- 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC: SRE ran targeted profiler and saw elevated iowait on nodes hosting customer slots
- 2026-03-10 11:15 UTC: Support requested customer to disable local streamer library; customer performed but initial tests were inconclusive
- 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC: reproducer run performed in staging with customer-provided library; I/O spike reproduced consistently

Observed behaviour: GPU scheduling/attach is delayed when the node NVMe I/O latency spikes above ~25ms; prefetch and snapshotter operations queue and the allocator's attach handshake times out twice before succeeding. This surfaces as prolonged slot acquisition followed by a short-lived throughput sag while the kernel services I/O.

Notes: This appears to be a customer-side process that writes high-frequency checkpoint/log files to the host NVMe. The library is configured by the customer to batch small writes and flush frequently which correlates with the observed IO pattern.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy customer sidecar image (dataweave/streamer:1.3.0-cust) on a dedicated node matching g-p4d-24.
2) Start a high-frequency micro-stream workload (1000 short requests/min) pinned to the customer's reserved pool.
3) Enable the streamer's local checkpointing (default config) that performs frequent small writes to /var/lib/streamer/checkpoints.
4) Observe node-level iostat and dstat: NVMe write latency rises to 20-60ms in bursts; simultaneously, watch allocator logs for 'attach timeout' messages and serving-runtime for 'slot reservation wait' events.
5) Disable local checkpoint writes and re-run: attach latency returns to baseline (~200-800ms).

investigation_notes: Initial triage: confirmed issue limited to customer's dedicated pool nodes (dwai-reserved-12). No host-level GPU driver faults or OOMs.
Correlated allocator attach timeouts with node NVMe iowait spikes via metric join (iowait >20ms windows aligned with attach retries).

Reproducer in staging using customer streamer image reproduced the same IO pattern and attach latency in a controlled test node. Hence root cause likely customer process writing small files to NVMe frequently.

Hypothesis A: customer-side library default flush frequency causes small-block synchronous writes; these saturate NVMe queue depth causing scheduler latencies and kernel blk updates; allocator attach waits on ephemeral metadata writes during slot attach.
Hypothesis B: sidecar container configured with hostPath for checkpoints without writeback throttling; containerized workload bypasses customer's intended rate-limiter.
Short test: disabled checkpointing in streamer config; attach latency dropped to baseline within 2 minutes — supports Hypothesis A.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-09 13:12: Thanks for the report — we've flagged this P1 and started collecting node-level IO stats. Can you confirm the sidecar image tag and whether local checkpointing was enabled?
Customer (DataWeaveAI) 2026-03-09 13:23: Confirmed: sidecar tag dataweave/streamer:1.3.0-cust and default checkpointing ON. We can toggle live if needed.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10 03:05: We see NVMe latencies in 20-60ms bursts coincident with allocator attach retries. Reproducer run pending with customer's image in staging.
Customer 2026-03-10 11:42: Disabled checkpointing flag and re-ran test — initial improvement but saw a few residual p99 blips. Will share additional logs.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-11 10:02: Reproducer confirms deterministic IO spikes caused by frequent small writes. Next: propose mitigation (rate-limiting writes, move to tmpfs, or change checkpoint strategy).
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-11 14:10 UTC): instructed customer to set STREAMER_CHECKPOINT_MODE=memory and reduce flush interval to 60s; immediate reduction in NVMe iowait observed and attach latencies returned to baseline across tests.

Permanent fix (plan): customer will ship a streamer patch that aggregates checkpoint writes to larger batches and exposes write_throttle configuration. Redwood SRE to verify patch via canary in staging before rolling to prod. ETA for rollout: 2026-03-18.

Platform mitigation: add allocator defensive circuit to extend attach retry backoff and detect sustained node-level IO pressure to avoid cascading attach retries. Engineering ticket created: INT-3304 (allocator IO-aware backoff).
Follow-ups: schedule a joint postmortem with DataWeaveAI after rollout; recommend documentation update for Dedicated customers describing safe disk usage patterns for sidecars.
